page: Amazon Web Services c6id.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor, the instance provides 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. Attached hardware resources include 2,850 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 19 Gbps. The underlying processor includes a 54 MB L3 cache and supports specialized vector and cryptographic instructions such as AVX-512, VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results show balanced compute output and isolated acceleration in instruction-specific tasks. In PassMark testing, the instance achieves strong results in cryptographic operations (43,659.0 points) alongside an average overall CPU score of 48,783.94 points. Similarly, Geekbench subtests indicate strong performance in ray tracing (50,081.0 points) and image processing (15,412.0 points), while clang software compilation reaches 37,035.0 points. Small-model LLM inference benchmarks demonstrate high processing efficiency, yielding 2,456.37 prompt tokens per second and 306.31 generation tokens per second on a 135M model, though larger models scale down predictably due to memory capacity and lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From an infrastructure perspective, the c6id.12xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for compute-bound systems requiring rapid local read/write capabilities. The inclusion of 2,850 GB of local NVMe storage eliminates the latency overhead associated with network-attached block storage for temporary data. However, workloads requiring high memory capacity per core are constrained by the 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance is suited for batch processing, media rendering, CI/CD build environments, high-throughput web serving, and distributed data processing pipelines that leverage direct NVMe scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 24-core, 48-thread Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory, offering a compute-aligned 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a bundled 2,850 GB local NVMe SSD and a baseline network throughput of 19 Gbps. Benchmark performance displays solid mid-range compute capability with above-average scores in cryptographic operations, image manipulation, and ray tracing due to AVX-512 and VAES hardware acceleration. The server lacks dedicated GPU hardware, but its combination of dedicated processor cores and high-speed local disk storage provides efficient throughput for disk-intensive batch tasks, media processing pipelines, automated code compilation, and analytics engines requiring high-performance scratch disk capacity.
